articles.title: Predictable AI spend in BigQuery: Introducing cost management for generative AI functions
articles.text:
The generative AI functions in BigQuery (AI.GENERATE, AI.IF, AI.CLASSIFY, AI.SCORE, and more) bring large language models (LLMs) directly into your SQL, so a single query can classify millions of support tickets or score each product review for sentiment. However, because these functions are billed by the token, scaling them across massive datasets highlights the importance of managing your budget proactively.
We recently announced the general availability (GA) of token-based cost management for BigQuery generative AI functions: daily quotas that let administrators set self-serve guardrails on AI token consumption, so teams can innovate while staying within your budget. In this blog, we provide an overview of cost management for BigQuery generative AI functions, walk through a few practical examples, and share resources to help you get started. Let’s jump in.
Quotas for managing costs
Four daily quotas, managed through the Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) quota system, provide controls at the project level and the per-user level. Per-user limits apply to each user within a project, not across your organization.
Quota name
Metric
Scope
Default value
AI input tokens per day
Input tokens used by the LLM
Per day, per project
200 billion
AI input tokens per day per user
Input tokens used by the LLM
Per day, per project, per user
150 billion
AI output tokens per day
Output and thinking tokens used by the LLM
Per day, per project, per project
20 billion
AI output tokens per day per user
Output and thinking tokens used by the LLM
Per day, per project, per user
15 billion
Key details:
The quotas are global. Usage is summed across all regions, so costs can't pile up unnoticed in a region you weren't watching.
Output quotas include "thinking" tokens. Reasoning tokens count toward your output quota, just as they count toward your Gemini platform bill.
Which functions are covered?
The quotas apply to these BigQuery functions that perform LLM-backed generation:
AI.GENERATE
AI.GENERATE_TABLE
AI.GENERATE_TEXT (and its alias ML.GENERATE_TEXT)
AI.CLASSIFY
AI.IF
AI.SCORE
AI.AGG
What's not covered: Embedding functions such as AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING (also available as ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING) and AI.EMBED are not subject to these quotas, because they run on different, substantially cheaper models.
Managing your quotas
Administrators can view and adjust the quotas directly in the Google Cloud console as workloads change, with no support case required.
Navigate to IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits.
Filter by service and select BigQuery API.
Sort by the Name column to bring the four AI quotas to the top.
Locating the gen AI token quotas in IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits.
4. Find the quota, for example AI input tokens per day.
5. Open the three-dot menu and choose Edit quota.
From there:
To tighten cost control, lower a quota. This takes effect immediately with no approval needed.
To support higher usage, request an increase from the same page. Many requests are auto-approved; larger increases may go through a quick review.
Editing a gen AI token quota in IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits.
You'll need the right permissions. You need one of: Owner, Editor, Quota Administrator (roles/servicemanagement.quotaAdmin), or Service Usage Admin (roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin).
Prefer automation? You can also manage these quotas programmatically through the Cloud Quotas API, the gcloud CLI, and Terraform to apply consistent guardrails across projects.
Monitoring usage
Beyond setting limits, the Quotas & System Limits page displays your historical token consumption so you can quickly detect spikes and right-size your budgets. Use these trends to see how new generative AI workloads and data pipelines affect your overall token usage.
Daily project-level token usage for a gen AI token quota in IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits.
Longer-term usage graph with selectable 7-day, 14-day, 30-day, and custom ranges.
For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the BigQuery documentation on controlling costs with token quotas.
Token quotas vs. billing spend caps
Token quotas aren't the only cost guardrail in Google Cloud.
Token quotas (this feature) are preventive and AI-specific. BigQuery tracks token usage during query execution and stops work close to the limit, with separate limits per project and per user.
Cloud Billing spend caps operate on dollars at the project and service level and can automatically block usage when a threshold is reached. They're a broad, financial backstop rather than a precise usage control, and because enforcement is not instant, some overages are incurred.
Use token quotas as your first line of defense for AI spend, and a spend cap as a project-wide safety net.
How enforcement works
Quotas are enforced by stopping work rather than letting a query run past your limit. A query is rejected up front with a QuotaExceeded error only if a quota it needs is already exhausted. Otherwise, it starts, and if a quota runs out mid-query, BigQuery stops sending new LLM calls:
Functions that support max_error_ratio (such as AI.IF) return partial results if unprocessed rows stay within the ratio, and otherwise fail.
General-purpose functions (such as AI.GENERATE) still succeed. Skipped rows have no generated value, and their status field contains the quota-exceeded error.
For details, see quota enforcement behavior in the documentation.
Sizing your input data: AI.COUNT_TOKENS
To choose quota values, it helps to know how much text your workloads send to a model. The AI.COUNT_TOKENS function helps with this.
AI.COUNT_TOKENS returns the number of tokens a model's tokenizer produces for a text string, without making a billable generation call. Run it over a column to measure your input data:
code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', "-- Count the input text tokens for each product review\r\nSELECT\r\n  SUM(\r\n    AI.COUNT_TOKENS(\r\n      CONCAT('Classify the sentiment of this review as positive, negative, or neutral: ', review_text),\r\n\r\n      endpoint => 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite').result) AS total_input_tokens\r\nFROM\r\n  `my_project.my_dataset.product_reviews`;"), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f84a72df310>)])]>
The count is a lower bound on input tokens. It doesn't include output or thinking tokens, the instructions each AI function adds around your input, or non-text inputs such as images. Use it to:
Gauge the input side of a workload before you launch it.
Right-size your quotas together with a small sample run that measures actual input and output usage.
Translate tokens into dollars using the published Gemini platform pricing for your model.
From tokens to budget: a worked example
Suppose you want to keep a project's daily AI spend around $100 with the Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite model. As of today's published pricing (BigQuery processes in batch which provides a 50% discount):
Input tokens: $0.125 per 1 million tokens
Output tokens (response + reasoning): $0.75 per 1 million tokens
If a small sample run shows an average 100:1 input-to-output token ratio, you can solve for a daily budget:
code_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('code', 'Cost:   0.125 × I + 0.75 × O = 100     (I, O in millions of tokens)\r\nRatio:  I = 100 × O'), ('language', ''), ('caption', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f84a65c58d0>)])]>
Solving gives about 754 million input tokens and 7.54 million output tokens per day. Set AI input tokens per day and AI output tokens per day to these values to hold the project near $100/day. If a project uses models with different prices, budget per model or blend the rates.
Best practices for managing AI cost
Start with per-user quotas. They stop one user or runaway experiment from draining the project's budget.
Measure before you scale. Use AI.COUNT_TOKENS to size your input, then check a small sample run in the usage chart before setting limits.
Mind the output side. Output tokens cost more. Where a function accepts max_output_tokens, set it to bound generation length.
Monitor and iterate. Adjust limits as real usage and budgets change.
Get started
Token-based cost management is available now. To begin:
Open IAM & Admin → Quotas & System Limits in the Google Cloud Console and filter by BigQuery API.
Review the four AI-related token quotas and set limits that match your budget.
Use AI.COUNT_TOKENS to size your input data.
For the full details, see the documentation on controlling generative AI costs.
With token-based guardrails in place, your teams can use generative AI in BigQuery with the cost predictability your organization needs.

articles.title: Samsung Expands Language Support Across AI Experiences on Galaxy
articles.text:
Samsung is expanding language support for Galaxy AI and Bixby, bringing these experiences to more users in their own language.
Galaxy AI is expanding language support across more of its features, starting with those that translate, transcribe, and summarize. Call Assist, Note Assist, Interpreter, and Transcript Assist now include Hungarian and Malay, bringing features such as Live Translate to 24 languages.1
▲ Live Translate of a phone call in Malay-English (Image simulated for illustrative purposes. Actual UX/UI may differ.)
Elsewhere in Galaxy AI, Now Nudge, which suggests a relevant next step based on what is on screen, adds eight languages2 to reach 24 as well.
Bixby is a device agent that offers intuitive device control through natural conversation. Users can ask for what they need in their own words, without having to know the exact name of a setting or where to find it in a menu. With the addition of Polish, Thai, and Vietnamese, Bixby now supports 12 languages,3 allowing more Galaxy users to control their devices more effortlessly.
Bixby’s new languages will begin rolling out on October 14,4 with the new Galaxy AI languages to follow in the coming weeks.5
Galaxy AI supports 24 languages: Arabic, Chinese (China mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan), Dutch, English (Australia, India, UK, U.S.), Filipino, French (Canada, France), German, Gujarati, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil, Europe), Romanian, Russian, Spanish (Mexico, Spain, U.S.), Swedish, Thai, Turkish, and Vietnamese. Regions in parentheses do not represent separate languages. ︎
Now Nudge adds Dutch, Filipino, Gujarati, Hungarian, Malay, Romanian, Swedish, and Turkish. ︎
Bixby service availability requires Samsung Account login and a data connection. Available functions and features may vary by country, region, and language. Bixby supports 12 languages: Chinese (China mainland), English (India, UK, U.S.), French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish (Latin America, Spain), Thai, and Vietnamese. Regions in parentheses do not represent separate languages. Other supported languages may be added in the future. Not all accents, dialects, and expressions are recognized, and actual performance may vary depending on pronunciation, voice level, and the surrounding environment. Use of Bixby may be limited in certain situations such as when recording media (Video/Game/Voice), during calls, and when using Maximum Power Saving mode, Emergency mode, and Samsung Kids. ︎
Detailed schedules and features may vary depending on the device or country. ︎
Some of the new Galaxy AI languages can be downloaded as language packs from the Settings app. ︎

articles.title: Cloud CISO Perspectives: New Gemini Notebook can help CISOs and policymakers prepare for PQC
articles.text:
Welcome to the first Cloud CISO Perspectives for October 2026. Today, Stephanie Kiel explains the latest on our approach to post-quantum cryptography, and shares a new tool to help CISOs and executives prepare their organizations for PQC.
As with all Cloud CISO Perspectives, the contents of this newsletter are posted to the Google Cloud blog. If you’re reading this on the website and you’d like to receive the email version, you can subscribe here.
aside_block
<ListValue: [StructValue([('title', 'Get vital board insights with Google Cloud'), ('body', <wagtail.rich_text.RichText object at 0x7f84a5fe0750>), ('btn_text', 'Visit the hub'), ('href', 'https://cloud.google.com/solutions/security/board-of-directors?utm_source=cgc-site&utm_medium=et&utm_campaign=FY26-Q2-GLOBAL-GCP39634-email-dl-dgcsm-CISOP-NL-177159&utm_content=-&utm_term=-'), ('image', <GAEImage: GCAT-replacement-logo-A>)])]>
New Gemini Notebook can help CISOs and policymakers prepare for PQC
By Stephanie Kiel, Head of Cloud Security Policy, Government Affairs and Public Policy, Google Cloud
Stephanie Kiel, Head of Cloud Security Policy, Government Affairs and Public Policy, Google Cloud
Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is one of the most urgent security shifts of the decade — and one of the easiest to tune out. For security leaders and policymakers, the research is dense, scattered across papers and engineering blogs, and can be challenging to turn into action.
To help, we're launching Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography, a public Gemini Notebook that brings Google's PQC research, engineering blogs, and migration guidance together in one place. Ask it questions, listen to an audio overview, or test yourself with flashcards, and quickly get up to speed on the quantum threat.
Why PQC matters now
Quantum computing is rapidly moving from theory to reality. Our Willow chip and Quantum Echoes algorithm mark substantial progress, and Google research estimates that breaking ECDLP-256 and RSA-2048 encryption — the public-key cryptography schemes protecting much of our online data — would require around 500,000 and 1 million imperfect quantum computer components (noisy qubits), respectively.
To help, we're launching Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography, a public Gemini Notebook that brings Google's PQC research, engineering blogs, and migration guidance together in one place.
This research has consequences now. It indicates that today’s online security is more vulnerable to future quantum computers than previously thought.
In Store Now, Decrypt Later attacks, adversaries may steal encrypted data now and wait to decrypt it once a sufficiently powerful quantum computer exists. Data that we’ve long considered sensitive — health records, financial data, intellectual property, and government secrets — is already at risk.
With continued advances in architecture, quantum algorithms, and quantum error correction shrinking future quantum hardware requirements, waiting to upgrade our digital locks is not a viable option. To help organizations stay ahead of the curve, Google has published a migration timeline noting our plans to transition to PQC by 2029, and we urge others to consider the same.
As the technology advances, policymakers should consider urging critical infrastructure owners and operators to recognize condensed timelines, and build PQC readiness into existing risk mitigation plans. We also recommend governments engage with global counterparts to promote a harmonized approach to standards development, and include technical and security experts in the building of policy and regulatory requirements focused on quantum safety.
Google's PQC expertise, in one notebook
The Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography notebook turns years of Google expertise into an interactive primer that anyone can use. It's built on curated Google sources covering the quantum era, quantum computing breakthroughs like Willow, Quantum Echoes, and surface code error suppression, industry PQC standards, Google's own deployments, and the latest research.
In the Gemini Notebook, you can:
Get answers grounded in Google's sources.
Listen to a podcast-style audio overview.
Test your PQC knowledge with flashcards.
Explore an interactive visual diagram of the quantum threat.
Read a concise briefing document.
Try these prompts
To get started, here are a few questions to ask the notebook:
For CISOs: "What should a CISO prioritize in the first 90 days of a PQC migration?"
For anyone new to PQC: "Explain store-now-decrypt-later in plain terms."
For developers: "How does hybrid ML-KEM key exchange work in Chrome?"
As with all generative AI, the notebook can make mistakes, so check its responses against the linked sources.
What's at stake
Previous cryptographic migrations, such as moving from SHA-1 or upgrading TLS, have taken a decade or more. Waiting for the availability of a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer before beginning the migration journey represents a significant security risk given the importance of public-key cryptography for securing digital essentials like web traffic, software updates, digital identities, and signatures.
For CISOs, we recommend that you start by:
Understanding where vulnerable cryptography lives in your organization.
Identifying and prioritizing data and systems most at risk from quantum threats, and developing a plan for addressing these risks.
Anticipate system-wide effects that PQC migration could have.
Building crypto-agility into your security plans, using learnings from past experiences like Heartbleed.
Additional detail on these recommendations is available in our previous blog post.
For the broader security community, the transition only succeeds if this knowledge is accessible to everyone — not just organizations with dedicated cryptography teams.
How Google is putting PQC into practice
We’ve been deploying PQC for years. Highlights include:
Hybrid Kyber/ML-KEM key exchange protecting Chrome traffic
PQC in Android
Quantum-safe digital signatures in Cloud KMS
PQC for Google's internal communications
Wiz PQC readiness scanner across code, cloud, and runtime
We also co-founded the Post-Quantum Cryptography Alliance at the Linux Foundation with industry leaders including Amazon Web Services, Cisco, IBM, and NVIDIA to support open-source tools like Open Quantum Safe.
Build a PQC notebook for your own team
Here’s how you can create a resource similar to our PQC Gemini Notebook, specific to your organization’s needs:
Curate trusted sources. Start with a focused set of authoritative research, standards, and guidance.
Write neutral prompts. Keep instructions factual so outputs stay grounded in your sources.
Add AI disclaimers and a welcome note. Tell readers what the notebook covers and remind them that AI can make mistakes.
Review all output with human oversight. Have experts check every artifact before you share it.
Start preparing today
The quantum transition has already started, but preparing your organization doesn't have to begin with a 100-page whitepaper. Start by understanding the threat, then assess your cryptographic inventory and build a migration roadmap.
You can get started with the Prepare for Post-Quantum Cryptography Gemini Notebook and share it with your team today. To learn more about Google Cloud’s approach to PQC, check out our dedicated Google Cloud PQC Resource Hub.

articles.title: European Cities Deploy NVIDIA-Powered AI Agents to Run Smarter Urban Operations
articles.text:
Keeping a city running means making decisions that affect residents every day — from when to repair a road to how to use energy more efficiently.
Across the EMEA region, cities and local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing to build physical AI agents and digital twins that help teams make those decisions. These applications can anticipate maintenance needs, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive.
Software partners including ABA Technology, Akila, Galene AI, Honeywell Technologies, K2K, Linker Vision, Milestone, Onetera, ThinkDeep and Younite AI are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/linker-vision.mp4
Video courtesy of Linker Vision.
NVIDIA Cosmos open models and the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) help agents interpret video and identify conditions, such as traffic congestion, equipment condition, underused spaces and safety hazards, that need attention. NVIDIA Nemotron open models enable developers to build agents that reason over information, respond in natural language and deploy digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.
Projects span Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, the U.K. and elsewhere.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
In the U.K., the Liverpool City Region, K2K is exploring how to build AI factories using NVIDIA accelerated computing, Cosmos and the VSS blueprint that can support urban planning and public services — testing applications for mobility and safety. The Island of Jersey is working with K2K to strengthen decision-making, mobility and urban planning while advancing clean energy and public services. Innovation City Belfast is exploring a pilot with K2K focused on smart mobility, transport systems, citizen safety and event and response management.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IKM®-�-Video-GTC-V.10.10.2-compressed.mp4
Video courtesy of K2K.
In France, the Department of Côte-d’Or, Akila and ThinkDeep built operations agents that combine sensor, infrastructure and historical data in a sovereign digital twin using NVIDIA Nemotron, Omniverse and accelerated computing, with Cosmos adoption planned for video data. Across more than 500 public buildings, the agents support energy, compliance, safety and climate resilience, and cut document search time from weeks to minutes and reduce total operating costs by 10%, targeting 30% at scale.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Akila-CGCO-compressed.mp4
Video courtesy of Akila.
In addition, Port Sud de France in Sète is working with ThinkDeep’s agentic platform that uses Cosmos and Nemotron to analyze cargo and safety data, coordinate operations and guide secure handling of hazardous materials.
In Italy’s Milan region, Galene.AI, Dell Technologies and TD Synnex are deploying an NVIDIA-powered, locally operated AI factory, starting with Cinisello Balsamo and planning expansion to four additional municipalities. Services include real-time translation, citizen chatbots and assistance with procurement and funding. These applications aim to simplify administrative work and help people get access to municipal data in seconds versus hours, while keeping local governance of data.
At Belgium’s Port of Antwerp-Bruges, Milestone and Dell Technologies are testing how agentic vision AI technologies, using NVIDIA Cosmos and the VSS blueprint, could support complex use cases such as oil-spill warnings by training models with synthetic data to prepare for incidents where real-world data is scarce.
In the Nordics, Younite AI is developing a digital twin experience with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for Gothenburg in Sweden as a part of the EU’s Citiverse initiative, focused on helping cities simulate changes and improve accessibility by providing event entrance previews, seating and crowd conditions before arrival.
These cities point toward a broader ambition: adapting agentic applications to local needs and extending them across departments and neighboring municipalities and countries such as Poland’s city of Wroclaw.
Elsewhere in the region, Honeywell Technologies is deploying Forge Cognition, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, Cosmos, Omniverse and the VSS blueprint, at the Dubai Fairmont Hotel to connect AI agents with building systems and improve reliability, energy efficiency and operations.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/honeywell.mp4
Video courtesy of Honeywell Technologies.
Building the AI Infrastructure for European Cities
For European cities, scaling from pilots to everyday operations requires infrastructure that can process local data, customize models and run AI agents.
System builders and infrastructure partners including Cisco, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are packaging NVIDIA accelerated computing, networking and storage into locally operated AI factories. These systems let cities customize and run intelligent applications locally while retaining control of their data, models and operations.
Nebius and Net Zero Compute are part of the broader ecosystem building AI factories designed to accelerate deployment and reduce costs for agentic services. EY and Accenture provide the integration and operational expertise to connect applications with city systems. Their work helps cities build repeatable deployment blueprints that they can adapt across departments and expand as local needs grow.
Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress, running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona.

NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem
articles.text:
Across industries, the U.K. is putting the full stack to work.
The scale of deployment is growing fast, from enterprises transforming their businesses to startups solving some of the planet’s hardest problems.
NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research.
NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK
NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research, Ineffable Intelligence, Synthesia, Wayve and many more.
Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz, Foresight, Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane.
Boltz, a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines.
Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue.
Hiverge, a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning.
Prima Mente, a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS.
Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use.
In addition, NVIDIA is partnering with the Earthshot Prize, joining as a Global Alliance Founding Partner to bring compute and technical expertise to innovators working on solutions for the world’s greatest climate and sustainability challenges.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
Technology Leaders Pioneer Intelligent Solutions Across the UK
In energy, Fuse Energy is moving its customer AI onto its own in-house infrastructure, built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra, delivering faster, more responsive support to over 450,000 U.K. households.
Meanwhile, sovereign AI company Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK — an open source dataset of one million synthetic personas representing the UK’s demographic, regional and cultural diversity — helping developers build fairer, more representative AI systems.
Healthcare
In healthcare, OneAdvanced is deploying what it calls the U.K.’s first and most advanced fine-tuned LLM for Primary Care AI-triage — built with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software and open models — supporting millions of National Health Service patients.
Heidi has now integrated NVIDIA Nemotron open models to give clinicians faster access to trusted medical evidence.
Speechmatics is deploying Oak, a multilingual medical speech recognition model, using NVIDIA Triton Inference — giving healthcare organizations control over where sensitive patient audio is processed.
Apian, Synnovis and NVIDIA are teaming up to use advanced computing and digital simulations using NVIDIA Cosmos to help hospital robots handle the heavy lifting of moving lab samples, freeing up medical staff to focus on patient care.
Danaher and NVIDIA are collaborating to advance autonomous science and help accelerate the pace of discovery by bringing accelerated computing, scientific and physical AI into laboratory workflows and instruments. Danaher’s recently announced AI-powered autonomous lab — designed to deliver up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents — is using NVIDIA BioNeMo open models within its AI-driven protein design workflows, data and automation technologies that connect design with experimental feedback.
Smart Cities
On the civic side, Liverpool City Region is building an NVIDIA-powered “City Brain” — a sovereign AI strategy designed as a blueprint for dozens of Unitary Authorities across the U.K.
Digital Jersey, Innovation City Belfast and Tees Valley Combined Authority are each exploring how trusted AI compute can serve communities and public services.
Financial Services
In financial services, LSEG and NVIDIA are bringing GPU-accelerated market analytics to global institutions.
Revolut introduced PRAGMA earlier in the year — a foundation model for banking event sequences, pre-trained on 26 million anonymised user histories. PRAGMA has moved from research to real-time scaling.
Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM, a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable AI. And Starling is developing a banking foundation model trained on Civo’s U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure.
NatWest is collaborating with NVIDIA on Nemotron Voice to better understand how banking customers across the U.K. speak, while Modulr is deploying a network of agents using Nemotron for distinct parts of payment operations.
Quantum
Quantum is moving from research to systems deployable alongside classical AI, and the U.K. is at the heart of this shift.
Riverlane has shown how GPUs can accelerate decoder recalibration workflows used in quantum error correction, helping decoder performance keep pace with real-time changes in quantum hardware behaviour. The work forms part of a broader collaboration exploring how AI, accelerated computing and quantum error-correction technologies can work together to support future quantum systems.
Together, these announcements showcase how enterprises, organizations and startups in the U.K. are fostering innovation across the nation. This includes more than 3,100 U.K. companies that are a part of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups.
Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST.
